ref_extractions.title: Age and sex modulate the variability of neural responses to naturalistic videos
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates age and sex effects on neural variability during naturalistic video watching using inter-subject correlation of EEG responses. While the authors (including several HBN investigators like Milham and Parra) conduct EEG research with developmental samples, the study predates the HBN-EEG release and does not reference or use the openneuro_ds005509 dataset specifically. It is a separate investigation of neural variability, not a task-based ML analysis on this dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=114 + N=303 replication cohort; investigates variability via inter-subject correlation; no specific ML task defined.

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the primary data descriptor paper for the HBN-EEG dataset infrastructure. It explicitly lists all nine dataset releases including https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds005509 as one of the HBN-EEG releases available on OpenNeuro. The paper describes the six paradigm tasks, HED annotations, and data quality procedures, providing essential documentation for the dataset.
ref_extractions.paradigm: mixed: resting-state, surround-suppression, movie-watching, sequence-learning, contrast-detection, symbol-search
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Not specified in this data descriptor; task-specific parameters expected in downstream analyses
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: This paper defines the infrastructure but does not itself perform ML tasks; it supports all downstream analyses on this dataset
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Explicitly lists ds005509 among nine HBN-EEG releases; describes all six tasks including sequence learning and contrast detection; N~2639 participants across releases.

ref_extractions.title: An open resource for transdiagnostic research in pediatric mental health and learning disorders
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes the broader HBN Biobank initiative (Alexander et al., 2017) including multimodal phenotyping, MRI, EEG, eye tracking, and genetics. While it mentions EEG as part of the biobank, it is not specific to the HBN-EEG dataset or release 5. It describes the rationale and design of the parent initiative rather than the specific EEG data structure.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: This is the parent biobank descriptor; the cited DOI (10.1038/sdata.2017.181) may serve as a general HBN citation but the paper does not specifically describe the EEG dataset used in analysis.md
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes HBN Biobank rationale, N=664 initial release; EEG mentioned as one modality among many; does not detail EEG paradigm or specific dataset release.

ref_extractions.title: A resource for assessing information processing in the developing brain using EEG and eye tracking
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the foundational methodological paper (Langer et al., 2017) describing the HBN EEG paradigm battery design including contrast detection, sequence learning, resting state, surround suppression, and video watching. The tasks match those described in analysis.md. However, it describes a pilot sample of N=126 subjects (ages 6-44), not the current N=330 release 5 dataset. It defines the paradigm but predates the specific HBN-EEG release.
ref_extractions.paradigm: contrast-detection, sequence-learning, symbol-search, resting-state, surround-suppression, movie-watching
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Not specified in paradigm descriptor; detailed experimental designs in original paradigm papers
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Paradigm design reference; may be cited alongside HBN-EEG infrastructure paper but N=126 pilot sample is not the current dataset
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes the six-task paradigm battery (3 active, 3 passive); N=126 pilot subjects; provides framework for HBN-EEG but precedes release 5.

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: PDF version of the HBN-EEG data descriptor paper. Explicitly lists all nine HBN-EEG dataset releases including ds005509 on OpenNeuro. Describes the BIDS format, HED event annotations, six tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, sequence learning, contrast detection, symbol search), and psychopathology dimensions. This is the key supporting document for the dataset.

ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N~2639 participants across nine releases; HED-annotated events; includes internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor dimensions.

ref_extractions.title: Automagic: Standardized preprocessing of big EEG data
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper (Pedroni, Bahreini, Langer, 2019) presents Automagic, a MATLAB toolbox for standardized EEG preprocessing and quality control. While it references the Healthy Brain Network as context for large-scale EEG initiatives, it does not use the openneuro_ds005509 dataset specifically. It is a methodology paper about preprocessing pipelines, not an analysis on this dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Methodology paper; references HBN as example of large-scale initiative but no specific dataset use; no ML task defined.

ref_extractions.title: Towards clinical applications of movie fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This perspective article (Eickhoff, Milham, Vanderwal, 2020) discusses the potential of movie fMRI for psychiatric imaging research. It focuses on fMRI methodology, advantages of naturalistic stimuli, and clinical applications. No EEG data is used, and the openneuro_ds005509 dataset (EEG) is not referenced.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: fMRI-focused perspective article; no EEG data; discusses movie-watching paradigms but not the HBN-EEG dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Functional connectivity of EEG is subject-specific, associated with phenotype, and different from fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper (Nentwich et al., 2020) analyzes EEG functional connectivity using phase-coupling (imaginary coherency) from the Healthy Brain Network Biobank (N=1657). It investigates associations with age, sex, IQ, ADHD, anxiety, and other phenotypes. While it uses HBN EEG data, it does not explicitly identify the specific openneuro_ds005509 dataset and the analysis focuses on FC rather than the ML classification/regression tasks described in analysis.md.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Not epoch-based; functional connectivity analysis across frequency bands
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses HBN data for FC analysis; phenotype associations but no explicit ML prediction task; does not name ds005509 specifically
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=1657 from HBN Biobank; phase-coupling (iCOH) analysis; associations with age, sex, IQ, ADHD, anxiety; across frequency bands.

ref_extractions.title: A benchmark for prediction of psychiatric multimorbidity from resting EEG data in a large pediatric sample
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper (Langer et al., 2022) proposes ML benchmark challenges using HBN EEG data: multi-task multi-label classification of seven DSM-V diagnoses and regression for symptom severity. It leverages the HBN initiative for psychiatric multimorbidity prediction. However, it does not explicitly reference the openneuro_ds005509 dataset or its specific release. The primary citation is the HBN biobank (Alexander et al., 2017), not the HBN-EEG infrastructure paper.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Resting state EEG epochs; exact epoch parameters depend on benchmark implementation
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses HBN data for ML benchmark; defines concrete classification (7 classes) and regression tasks; does not explicitly name ds005509
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=2042 from HBN initiative; 7 DSM-V diagnoses (multi-label); psychiatric symptom severity regression; resting EEG + demographics only.

ref_extractions.title: The Coronavirus Health and Impact Survey (CRISIS) reveals reproducible correlates of pandemic-related mood states across the Atlantic
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper (Nikolaidis et al., 2021) presents the CoRonavIruS Health and Impact Survey (CRISIS), a questionnaire-based study about mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. It uses online survey data (N=5646) collected via Prolific Academic. No EEG data is used, no neuroimaging dataset is involved, and the openneuro_ds005509 dataset is completely unrelated to this study.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Questionnaire-based survey study; no EEG; no neuroimaging; COVID-19 mental health focus.
